latest_rss.title: Central Asia’s Border Regime Creates New Distance and Connection
latest_rss.summary:
Executive Summary:




Central Asian states continue to improve border management through ongoing cooperation. “Invisible borders” are nevertheless manifesting in official policies, communiqués, and speeches that could quietly sabotage regional ties and large-scale development plans.



Geopolitical rapprochement in Central Asia is gaining traction, but the coordination and implementation of “soft” infrastructure remain sluggish. New border regimes create new forms of distantiation even as they forge new connectivities.



Regional cooperation through mechanisms that foster bottom-up initiatives, transparency, and sustainability of multilateral projects will help address shared challenges. Invisible borders are neither new nor insurmountable in the pursuit of institutional cohesion on the way to regionalism.

latest_rss.title: Ukrainian Attacks Leading Russian Corporations to Mull Moving Out of Moscow
latest_rss.summary:
Executive Summary:




Ukrainian drone attacks on Moscow and the prospect of ballistic missile strikes are prompting firms to consider relocating for their own safety to regions east of the Urals and thus further from where such strikes can be launched.



Some in Moscow and more in Russia’s regions are not opposed to such moves, in the first case because it supports Russian President Vladimir Putin’s turn toward the People’s Republic of China and in the second because it improves their situations. Most in both would prefer it to be planned rather than forced.



The number and size of the firms involved are still small, but if Ukrainian attacks continue and intensify, their impact will grow, affecting not only Russia’s currently hyper-centralized economy but also its equally centralized political system.
